response.justification: The candidate is an experienced full-stack software engineer (15+ years) with strong web, backend, and some low-latency systems work, but the role requires deep hardware-domain expertise that is entirely absent from the resume. There is no evidence of SoC/IP modeling, RTL or architectural simulation, GPU/accelerator architecture, SIMD/MIMD design, deep-learning workload optimization, or hardware-software co-design. The only adjacent experience is C/C++ work at National Instruments (7 months, IDE tooling) and some embedded/robotics integration at Altom, neither of which approaches principal-level performance architecture for AI accelerators. Educationally, a BS in CS with 8+ years does meet the baseline path, but the technical domain mismatch is decisive.
strengths: 15+ years of software engineering across web, mobile, desktop and embedded
Low-latency, high-throughput systems experience (async I/O, fibers, caching at Sociomantic)
Strong engineering rigor: TDD, CI/CD, open-source tooling, public talks and workshops
concerns: No SoC/IP modeling, RTL, or hardware architecture simulation experience
No AI accelerator, GPU architecture, SIMD/MIMD, or DNN training/inference optimization background
Career trajectory is application/full-stack focused, not principal-level hardware performance architecture

key_factors.factor: Missing SoC/IP modeling and hardware architecture expertise
No AI accelerator / GPU / deep-learning workload experience
Extensive general software engineering seniority and systems performance work
